key_insight: Black participation in landmark hypertrophic cardiomyopathy trials was far below expectation, with only 3.98% of Black-or-White participants recorded as Black versus a 16.3% population expectation.
clinical_relevance: Underrepresentation in pivotal HCM trials may limit how well trial findings reflect real-world patients, especially for Black communities affected by delayed specialist care and worse outcomes.
method: Reviewed 197 registered interventional HCM trials and identified 32 landmark-tier studies; demographic data were extractable for 16 and race reporting for 13.
Compared pooled Black participation against three benchmarks: US adult population, trial site-catchment counties, and a disease-referenced echocardiographic expectation.
Tested whether geography and quantitative eligibility thresholds could explain the enrollment gap using site addresses, census data, and NHANES.
evidence_signal: Across 13 trials, 70 of 1,780 Black-or-White participants were Black; pooled Black share was 3.98% and the participation-to-prevalence ratio was 0.24, with all trials below catchment-based expectations.
watch_item: Interpretation is limited by incomplete race reporting and by the fact that geography and eligibility thresholds may not capture other structural barriers to enrollment.
paper_title: Race and ethnicity in the landmark hypertrophic cardiomyopathy trials: representation against population, site-catchment, and disease-referenced expectations
